note: Frozen before any STEP 5-3 pilot or main run. The evaluation must use this preregistration; a change requires a new version with a recorded reason.

preregistration.version_note: v3: user decisions 1-7 (2026-11-13) incorporated; expanded A units adopted
preregistration.scope: Tests whether the residual state of the last input token (h_q, the token that predicts the answer) at one decoder layer carries information specific to the image set that changes the answer. h_q is patched between two orders of the same images (a non-last N position answered Yes, the N-last order answered No) and compared with a condition-matched donor from a different image set. Images and baseline outputs are reused from STEP 5-2 / 5-2b: this is a selection / confirmation split of existing data, not an independent test on new images.

data.split: selection / confirmation halves by N image ID, seed 53 (configs/data/step5_causal_split.yaml)
data.units: Expanded definition (adopted by the user, 2026-11-13). Same series (one N image x one strength) and same image count n in {3, 4, 5}: an input with N at a non-last position a (first a = 0 or middle) answered Yes (False-Yes) and the N-last input of the same series and n answered No (Correct-No) in the 5-2b main run. 1,186 units (390 first + 796 middle; n = 3: 351, 4: 404, 5: 431) from 313 N images; about 590 per half.
data.baseline_answers: parsed answers of the 5-2b main run, fixed before any 5-3 output; inclusion never uses 5-3 outputs

intervention.site: Output (residual stream) of decoder layer l at the last input token, i.e. the input of decoder layer l + 1 (l = 0 is the embedding output; l = 36 is the input of the final norm).
intervention.operation: Replace the recipient's value at the site with the donor's value at the same site. The donor value comes from the donor's own no-intervention run on the same computation path. All other positions and layers are unchanged. Greedy generation (max_new_tokens 8, the model's generation config including its repetition penalty 1.05, as in the baseline extraction) continues from the patched state.
intervention.layers_run: l = 0..36 (l = 1..36 is the sweep; l = 0 and l = 36 also serve as integrity checks)

directions.restore: recipient = the False-Yes input of a unit; same-set donor = the unit's N-last Correct-No input; target answer No
directions.contaminate: recipient = the unit's N-last Correct-No input; same-set donor = the unit's False-Yes input; target answer Yes

intervention.control_donor_C1: An input of a different N image in the same half with the same class and image count (identical prompt), the same N position and the same baseline answer as the same-set donor (restore: N-last answered No; contaminate: N at the same a answered Yes). Among candidates, the one whose total input token count is closest to the recipient's; remaining ties are broken by a seeded draw (seed 53, units in sorted order). One C1 donor per unit and direction, recorded in the plan before any GPU run. Units without a candidate are excluded from that direction's primary contrast and counted.
intervention.computation: Fast path: the prefix (all tokens before the last input token) is computed once per recipient with a KV cache; the last token is recomputed for all conditions of a unit and direction in one batch, with the no-intervention row in the same batch.

outcomes.answer_parsing: as STEP 5-2 (greedy, max_new_tokens 8, strip, trailing punctuation removed, case-folded)
outcomes.success: restore: parsed answer No; contaminate: parsed answer Yes; unparsed is not a success
outcomes.change_rate: share of units with a success
outcomes.margin: fp32 variant margin (as STEP 5-2). Delta margin = patched margin minus the no-intervention margin of the same batch.

layer_selection.data: selection half only; units that have a C1 donor in that direction
layer_selection.candidates: l = 1..35. l = 36 is excluded because both donors then reproduce their own answer, so the difference is 0 by construction; l = 0 is an identity check.
layer_selection.score: S(l) = (number of units with a success under the same-set donor) - (number under the C1 donor); integer counts
layer_selection.rule: per direction: l*_restore = argmax S_restore(l), l*_contaminate = argmax S_contaminate(l); ties -> the smallest l
layer_selection.non_positive: if max S(l) <= 0, l* is still chosen by the rule and the confirmation decision proceeds unchanged (reported)
layer_selection.record: written to selection.json (with a SHA-256 of its content) by the evaluation code before any confirmation-half value is computed

A-H1.name: restoration specificity
A-H1.statement: At l*_restore, the same-set donor turns False-Yes into No more often than the C1 donor.
A-H1.estimate: mean over confirmation-half units of [success(same-set donor) - success(C1 donor)] at l*_restore
A-H1.weighting: each unit equal weight; image counts 3-5 and positions (first, middle) pooled

A-H2.name: contamination specificity
A-H2.statement: At l*_contaminate, the same-set donor turns Correct-No into Yes more often than the C1 donor.
A-H2.estimate: mean over confirmation-half units of [success(same-set donor) - success(C1 donor)] at l*_contaminate
A-H2.weighting: each unit equal weight (an N-last recipient enters once per unit); image counts and positions pooled

hypotheses.note: A-H1 and A-H2 are decided separately; neither changes any STEP 5-2 / 5-2b decision.

minimum_effect.rationale: The answer change rate is the primary outcome because the margin gap between the two orders of a pair is small (median 0.71-0.94 logit by image count, 0.84 overall), which makes a logit-scale minimum effect too strict. Projected 97.5% CI half-width per half with the expanded units: 0.08-0.10 with within-N-image correlation 0.3 (0.05-0.15 for correlation 0-1; variance of the paired difference 0.30-0.48; 5.4 units per N image weighted).

decision.level: 97.5% intervals (Bonferroni for two primary hypotheses), N-image cluster bootstrap

A-H1.supported: estimate >= 0.15 AND N-image cluster 97.5% CI lower bound > 0
A-H1.robust_label: 'robust support' only if the class cluster 97.5% CI lower bound is also > 0; otherwise 'support (cross-class generalization uncertain)'

A-H2.supported: estimate >= 0.15 AND N-image cluster 97.5% CI lower bound > 0
A-H2.robust_label: 'robust support' only if the class cluster 97.5% CI lower bound is also > 0; otherwise 'support (cross-class generalization uncertain)'

statistics.method: percentile cluster bootstrap; 97.5% for A-H1 / A-H2, 95% for secondary and descriptive results (labelled)
statistics.resampling_unit: the unit's N image ID, within the confirmation half; C1 donors stay fixed

descriptive.single_layer: l*_joint = argmax [S_restore(l) + S_contaminate(l)] on the selection half (same candidates and tie rule); its value and both directions' confirmation-half contrasts at l*_joint (95%), descriptive only.
descriptive.earliest_half_restore: per half: the earliest l (1..36) at which the restore change rate under the same-set donor is >= 0.5 ('none' if no layer reaches it); the same value under the C1 donor for comparison.
descriptive.layer_curves: change rates for both donors and the difference at every l, both directions and both halves; confirmation-half layers other than l* are exploratory.

secondary.by_position: A-H1 and A-H2 contrasts for first-position units (= the original N-first-only definition) and middle-position units, at l*
secondary.per_count: the same contrasts for 3, 4 and 5 images
secondary.margin: Delta margin contrast (same-set minus C1) at l*, fp32 variant and bf16 margins
secondary.all_positive_side_effect: For the same series and image counts as the units, the two 5-2 All-P orders (N slot first / last) are patched into each other at every l; reported at l*_restore and l*_contaminate on the confirmation half: share of recipients answering Yes without intervention whose answer becomes No, and Delta margin.
secondary.sensitivity: contrasts repeated (1) without units whose recipient's no-intervention answer differs from the baseline answer and (2) without units whose recipient's baseline bf16 margin sign disagrees with the baseline answer (ties included)

interpretation: The same-set donor differs from the recipient in image order, so set-specific and order information are not separated.
The C1 donor has a different total token count (closest chosen); its value is placed at the recipient's last position.
First and middle positions are pooled; the 5-2b middle - first False-Yes difference was inconclusive (+0.04).
Images and baseline outputs are reused (selection / confirmation split), not an independent test on new images.
integrity_checks: no-intervention fast path reproduces the 5-2b / 5-2 baseline answers and margins: parsed answer agreement >= 0.99 and |fp32 variant margin difference| <= 0.25 in >= 99% of inputs (else stop)
fast path vs reference path (model.generate full prefill with the same patch) on every pilot row: same thresholds (else stop)
l = 0 patch equals the no-intervention row of the same batch within the same thresholds (the last input token is the same token in every input); the exact-equality share is reported
l = 36 patch reproduces the donor's no-intervention fp32 variant margin within 0.01 in every row, and its parsed answer in >= 99% of rows
image token spans identical to the baseline runs (checked for every input before running)
run.json records GPU type, driver, CUDA and library versions
reported_not_decided: answer agreement excluding inputs whose baseline bf16 margin is within one bf16 step (|margin| <= 0.125): 3.6% of 5-2b inputs are exact bf16 Yes/No ties (resolved as No by the lower token id) and 11% are within one step, so a different but correct computation path can break such ties differently

rules: any integrity criterion fails (pilot or main)
estimated main-run time from measured pilot times exceeds the limit
